_comment: The golden WALKTHROUGH reel (REFERENCE_STYLE_ADDENDUM.md section 3B): docs/reference/tokenization-reel.mp4's story and objects, CUT to the addendum's rules — 4 chapters instead of the reel's 6 (steps 5 and 6, padding and vectors, are left for a Part 2), about 80 s instead of 194 s, one sentence per caption, and one running example ('Tokenization matters.') whose state carries from each chapter into the next. Source: content/tokenization_basics.md, written from the reel's narration because content/ had no tokenization material. Also the stub answer for SYSTEM_MOTION_WALKTHROUGH when the material teaches tokenization (shorts/stubs.py).
topic: How does an AI model read your text?
hook_question: How does AI read your text?

chapters.title: Swap each token for a number

shots.speech: How does AI read your text? It can't. It only reads numbers.
shots.visual: Navy field. KineticTitle 'HOW DOES AI READ YOUR TEXT?' builds word by word; type_scatter into 'IT CAN'T.' in coral; then 'IT ONLY READS' over a framed 'NUMBERS.' on a falling-digit TextureBackground.

shots.speech: Turning words into numbers is called tokenization.

captions.text: Turning words into numbers is called tokenization.

shots.visual: iris into the blue field. 'WORDS' with an arrow_draw down to 'NUMBERS' (text_scramble settles the digits into the word); then type_assemble builds 'TOKENIZATION' under a 'THIS IS CALLED' label.

shots.speech: Let's follow one sentence: Tokenization matters. Just two words.
shots.visual: Blue field, label 'FOLLOW ONE SENTENCE'. typewriter_cursor types the sentence; two word boxes with number badges 1 and 2.
bar_wipe into the paper field. ChapterCard: 'STEP 1 OF 4', '01', 'Cut the sentence'; the number flies into the step chip.

shots.speech: The tokenizer cuts at spaces and punctuation. The full stop becomes its own piece.

captions.text: The full stop becomes its own piece.

shots.visual: Paper field, step chip 01. A cut marker sweeps the sentence; TokenRow splits into 'Tokenization' 'matters' '.'; a BigCounter '3 PIECES'.
iris out of the '3' into the navy field. ChapterCard: 'STEP 2 OF 4', '02', 'Check the word shelf'.

shots.speech: Every model has a fixed list of word pieces it knows, called its vocabulary. Ours knows about 1.2 lakh pieces.

captions.text: Every model has a fixed list of word pieces it knows, called its vocabulary.

shots.visual: Navy field. LookupGrid 'THE SHELF' with grid_cascade (12 readable cells, the rest as texture); count_up to 1,20,000 in a framed BigCounter while the grid dims.

shots.speech: Matters is on the shelf, but tokenization is not. So it is built from smaller pieces.

captions.text: “Matters” is on the shelf, but “tokenization” is not.
So it is built from smaller pieces.

shots.visual: Navy field. Zoom into the 'matters' cell with an 'ON THE SHELF' tag; then search_type 'Tokenization' with the scan line; Stamp 'NOT ON THE SHELF'.

shots.speech: Token? Not on the shelf. It takes the longest piece that fits: To, then ken, then ization.

captions.text: It takes the longest piece that fits: To, then ##ken, then ##ization.

shots.visual: double_bar_wipe into the paper field. Shelf row on top; scan_window over 'Tokenization' with a NO tag shrinks to 'To' (YES), a connector draws to the shelf; then 'ken' and 'ization' match the same way and drop to the result row.
stack_rise into the blue field. ChapterCard: 'STEP 3 OF 4', '03', 'Add special tokens'.

shots.speech: CLS goes at the front, and SEP goes at the end. Two words are now seven tokens.

captions.text: [CLS] goes at the front, and [SEP] goes at the end.

shots.visual: Blue field. chip_insert slides lavender [CLS] and [SEP] into the ends of the token row; BigCounter '7 TOKENS'.

shots.speech: Why? The model gathers a summary of the whole sentence into CLS.

captions.text: The model gathers a summary of the whole sentence into [CLS].

shots.visual: Blue field. ghost_word 'WHY?' behind the row; a Bracket labels [CLS] 'SUMMARY SEAT' and dots flow into it.
diagonal_stripes (yellow + the new field) into the yellow field. ChapterCard: 'STEP 4 OF 4', '04', 'Swap each token for a number'.

shots.speech: Every shelf piece has a fixed ID, like a roll number in class.

captions.text: Every shelf piece has a fixed ID, like a roll number in class.

shots.visual: Yellow field. LookupTable ID / TOKEN with a highlighted row above the token row.

shots.speech: For example, CLS is 101. The number has no meaning by itself.

captions.text: The number has no meaning by itself.

shots.visual: Yellow field. slot_scroll stops on [CLS] = 101; each chip swaps to its ID in turn.

shots.speech: So two words became seven tokens, and then seven numbers.

captions.text: So two words became seven tokens, and then seven numbers.

shots.visual: bar_wipe into the blue field. counter_morph '2 → 7' (WORDS, TOKENS); the ID row below.

shots.speech: So always count tokens with your model's own tokenizer.

captions.text: So always count tokens with your model's own tokenizer.

shots.visual: Blue field. KineticTitle 'COUNT TOKENS WITH YOUR MODEL'S OWN TOKENIZER.' with 'TOKENIZER.' in yellow.

shots.speech: Tokenization in four steps: cut, check the shelf, add special tokens, swap in numbers.

captions.text: Tokenization in four steps: cut, check the shelf, add special tokens, swap in numbers.

shots.visual: stack_rise into the navy field. RecapGrid 'Tokenization in 4 steps' with the four chapter titles; the final ID row underneath.

shots.speech: Follow for more, one idea at a time.

captions.text: Follow for more, one idea at a time.

shots.visual: Navy field. End card: Up next, Follow button.
